chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Najran, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him: A group of people act in disobedience and say, 'We hope,' and they remain in that state until death comes to them. He said: These are a people who sway in their expectations (of mercy); they are lying. They are not truly hoping. Indeed, whoever hopes for something seeks it, and whoever fears something flees from it.

key_terms.الْأَمَانِيُّ: expectations or hopes (often implying vague or unearned expectations)
key_terms.يَتَرَجَّحُونَ: sway or vacillate (between hope and despair)

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between hope (rajā') and action in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) critiques the complacency of those who rely on hope without action, defining true hope as an active pursuit of the desired goal and true fear as a flight from danger. This hadith establishes the Shia principle that hope (rajā’) and fear (khawf) are not passive emotions but dynamic forces that must manifest in corresponding deeds to be valid. It serves as a corrective to the Murji'ah view of faith, emphasizing that hope without effort is merely 'delusion' (tarajjūh fī al-amānī).
